title: Naturality of the canonical derived tensor-Hom equivalence
statement: For morphisms in each of the three variables, the canonical derived tensor-Hom equivalence commutes with precomposition in the first two variables and postcomposition in the third.

source.place: Tag 08DJ, naturality of the canonical tensor-Hom map

proof.text: Write $e_{K,L,M}$ for the family of [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection] on $D(\mathcal O_X)$ for a scheme $X$. That definition chooses a family natural in all three variables. Explicitly, for $a:K\to K_0$, $b:L\to L_0$, $c:M_0\to M$ and $f:K_0\to R\mathcal Hom(L_0,M_0)$, naturality is the equality $e_{K,L,M}(R\mathcal Hom(b,c)\circ f\circ a)=c\circ e_{K_0,L_0,M_0}(f)\circ(a\otimes^L b)$. Both sides are morphisms $K\otimes^L L\to M$. Thus this equality is the naturality property already required of the chosen canonical family, with no further existence assertion. For the first variable, set $b=1_L$ and $c=1_M$ to obtain $e_{K,L,M}(f\circ a)=e_{K_0,L,M}(f)\circ(a\otimes^L1_L)$. For the second, set $a=1_K$ and $c=1_M$ to obtain $e_{K,L,M}(R\mathcal Hom(b,1_M)\circ f)=e_{K,L_0,M}(f)\circ(1_K\otimes^L b)$. For the third, set $a=1_K$ and $b=1_L$ to obtain $e_{K,L,M}(R\mathcal Hom(1_L,c)\circ f)=c\circ e_{K,L,M_0}(f)$. These substitutions use the identity laws for the tensor and internal-Hom functors; the displayed simultaneous formula proves compatibility for arbitrary $a,b,c$.

lean.statement:
theorem schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv_naturality (Y : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (K K' L L' M M' : schemeDerivedCategory Y)
    (a : K' ⟶ K) (b : L' ⟶ L) (c : M ⟶ M')
    (g : K ⟶ (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.sheaf).obj
      (op L, M)) :
    schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv Y K' L' M'
        (a ≫ g ≫ (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) Y.sheaf).map
          (b.op, c)) =
      (a ⊗ₘ b) ≫ schemeDerivedTensorHomEquiv Y K L M g ≫ c
